Maya (eng-runtime): quick follow-up from the ops run — continuous batcher is great for throughput but we saw some surprising p99 regressions on tiny requests (single-token open-loop traces).
Liam (eng-runtime): yikes. do we have a repro trace or a short log?
Maya (eng-runtime): yes — attached a few condensed traces in the paste. key pattern: high compaction -> longer wait time for first token when request size = 1.
Sophia (eng-runtime): is this the micro-window tradeoff? i.e., we increase compactness (bigger window) to get packing efficiency but that increases queuing delay for short requests.
Maya (eng-runtime): exactly. throughput up ~12% but p99 up 40–60ms on single-token flows.
Ethan (eng-platform): what's the traffic mix? if most requests are multi-token, maybe overall SLA still ok.
Maya (eng-runtime): traffic mix is bimodal. about 30% short (<=3 tokens), 50% medium, 20% long. Short ones are latency-sensitive endpoints (chat heartbeats, quick completions).
Liam (eng-runtime): we could special-case short requests with a fastpath: no batching, or very tiny micro-window. but that reduces packing and hurts throughput.
Henry (eng-ml): also consider prefix/KV cache warmup — short requests don't benefit from KV caching and sometimes get preempted by larger batches that thrash GPU memory regions.
Sophia (eng-runtime): idea: latency budget hints per request. clients provide deadline hint, we assign to low-latency lane when deadline tight. similar to lane fencing but simpler.
Maya (eng-runtime): liked that. but worry about exploitation by tenants and fairness. need admission credits + weight adjustments.
Liam (eng-runtime): could be enforced server-side: if request small we synthesize a default deadline hint based on endpoint profile. no client changes.
Ethan (eng-platform): how about dynamic windowing: adjust micro-window size per aggregate short-request rate. if short rate spikes, shrink window. When it falls, expand to reclaim efficiency.
Sophia (eng-runtime): that was attempted in alpha: oscillation issues when rates are noisy. we added hysteresis but still had slow reaction to sudden spikes.
Maya (eng-runtime): logs show the slow reaction came from averaging over 10s. we could do two-tier metrics: short-window fast estimator (1s) + stable estimator (30s) and control with blend.
Henry (eng-ml): don't forget KV cache headroom. when window shrinks, more concurrent batches may be inflight and KV cache pressure increases. we need a headroom reservation algorithm to avoid thrash.
Liam (eng-runtime): proposal sketch: 1) classify requests by token-count and endpoint hint; 2) maintain per-class micro-window; 3) fast estimator for sudden shifts; 4) per-GPU KV headroom reservation proportional to concurrent lanes; 5) enforcement: small requests hit fast lane unless they exceed rate quota.
Maya (eng-runtime): + add a cheap admission token in enqueue path so we can cheaply reject/route if fast lane overloaded. tiny token check (atomic counter). keeps enqueue O(1).
Sophia (eng-runtime): needs telemetry flags: per-lane p50/p95/p99, pack efficiency, kv-eviction-rate. that will let us tune hysteresis and headroom.
Ethan (eng-platform): operational concerns: config knobs exposed in console (target latency, min window, max window, fastlane capacity) and a safe default autoscaler. also rollout in canary with canary endpoints.
Liam (eng-runtime): edge-case: many small requests from a single tenant could monopolize fast lane. enforcement: per-tenant fastlane quota + burst credits.
Henry (eng-ml): also evaluate model-sensitivity: some models suffer quality drop when micro-batching changes ordering/temperature—need evaluation harness checks for regression during rollouts.
Maya (eng-runtime): next steps: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with the sketch above + a short experiment plan (canary config, telemetry, safety knobs).
Sophia (eng-runtime): can you include the quick code snippet for the atomic admission token? small patch we can test fast.
Maya (eng-runtime): sure. paste: ```// enqueue fast lane
if (fastlane_counter.load() >= fastlane_capacity) {
  // fallback to regular queue or reject
  goto regular_queue;
}
fastlane_counter.fetch_add(1);
enqueue_fastlane(item);
```
Liam (eng-runtime): minor: use compare_exchange in hot paths to avoid overshoot under contention.
Maya (eng-runtime): good call. I'll include that.
Ethan (eng-platform): timeline? Ops wants an experiment this week. can we slice a canary endpoint?
Maya (eng-runtime): target: small canary by EOD Friday. RFC draft tomorrow.
InfraBot: deployment note — canary env ci-42 has 2 GPUs reserved; will open a canary channel when ready.
Sophia (eng-runtime): ack. I'll help instrument telemetry dashboards (per-lane p99 + pack-eff).
Henry (eng-ml): I'll add a small eval that runs short-request mixes to assert no quality regressions.
Maya (eng-runtime): thanks. wrapping up: aim is to regain p99 for short requests without losing >6% throughput. will track 1) p99 short, 2) overall TPS, 3) pack-eff, 4) kv-evictions.
Liam (eng-runtime): sounds good. keep updates here.
Maya (eng-runtime): thanks team :pray:
